highlights:
1M to $100M Run Rate in 4 Quarters

 NOV 03 2026 // 3 min read 

# 1M to $100M Run Rate in 4 Quarters

...

F our quarters. That is how long it took us to go from a $1M run rate to $100M. This year alone, we grew 37.5x. I keep staring at those numbers. They still do not feel real.

...

Daytona goes from 1M to $100M run rate in 4 quarters.

...

The short version: agents need somewhere to run.

Models think on GPUs. Work happens on CPUs. Every time an agent writes code, opens a browser, installs a package, or forks a long-running job, it needs a machine; isolated, fast, stateful, and available through an API. The cloud we already had was built for human-shaped workloads: start a VM, wait, run the same thing the same way. Agents do not work like that. They spin up thousands of environments. They pause and resume. They explore branches in parallel. They need startup in tens of milliseconds, not minutes.

...

What came back was an unmistakable pull. People building agents did not want a demo box. They wanted a real computer for every agent: code execution, computer use, reinforcement learning, the messy stuff in between. This is what Daytona is, an Agent Execution Cloud. Instantaneous startup times, state that persists. Forks and snapshots. Per-second billing that matches how agents actually use compute.

results.title: PTY keepalive pings and Android sandbox class removal
highlights:
OCT 05 2026

# PTY keepalive pings and Android sandbox class removal

Daytona 0.222.0 removes the android sandbox class from the API client, keeps PTY sessions alive with WebSocket pings, and cleans up temp files after downloads in the Go SDK and CLI.

### Features

API client: remove the android sandbox class

### Fixes

SDK: send WebSocket keepalive pings on PTY sessions

Go SDK, CLI: remove temp files left behind by file and recording downloads

### Chores

Go SDK: bump to v0.222.0
